title: Final: where data lives
sub: Everything about types and memory: test yourself
cards/0/q: Size is a struct. What is a.W?
cards/0/explain: A struct is copied whole: b is an independent copy.
cards/1/q: And if Size is a class?
cards/1/explain: For a class, the reference is copied: a and b are one object.
cards/2/q: What ends up on the heap? Select all that apply.
cards/2/options/2: An int field inside a class instance
cards/2/explain: Class instances, everything inside them, and boxes from boxing live on the heap. Local value-type variables live on the stack.
cards/3/q: Point is a class, p = (5, 5). What happens to p.X after the call?
cards/3/explain: The method replaced its own copy of the reference. Without ref, the variable p doesn't change.
cards/4/explain: The box holds an int. You can only unbox to int and convert afterwards: (double)(int)o.
cards/5/explain: ToUpper returns a new string, and the result is thrown away. The program prints "hi!".
cards/6/q: An array of 100 Point class instances, all filled. How many objects are on the heap?
cards/6/explain: The array itself plus 100 separate points.
cards/7/explain: With ref, the method works with the variable n itself.
cards/8/q: A method returned. What disappeared immediately?
cards/8/options/0: Its stack frame with all local variables
cards/8/options/2: Nothing; the garbage collector cleans up everything
cards/8/explain: The frame is discarded instantly. Objects on the heap live as long as something references them.
cards/9/pairs/3/1: Boxing: a box on the heap
cards/10/q: Pass a big struct without copying it and without permission to change it
